markdown:
Jury duty is the only civic obligation most Americans will ever be compelled to perform, and most of them try to get out of it. I understand the impulse. The summons arrives at a bad time, the pay is forty dollars a day, and the parking is is never free.

But the jury is the one place where the state must persuade twelve ordinary people before it can take someone's liberty. That is not a procedural detail. It is a principal, and it is the reason the Sixth Amendment exists.

If you want to know what your government is like, spend a week in a courtroom watching it try to prove something.
